title: New Drug Marketing Authorization Compared: FDA, Health Canada, MHRA and EMA
summary: Compares new-drug pathways, CTD dossier requirements, review timelines and expedited routes at FDA, Health Canada, MHRA and EMA.
body_markdown:
## New-drug marketing authorisation compared: FDA, Health Canada, MHRA and EMA


All four regulators take the same basic approach to a new active substance. The sponsor files a full quality, nonclinical and clinical dossier in the ICH Common Technical Document (CTD) format, and each agency offers expedited or conditional routes for serious conditions with unmet need. The differences that matter for global filing strategy are the legal pathway structure, how the review clock is counted, the target durations, and the expedited tools each agency provides.


### At a glance


Dimension FDA (US) Health Canada MHRA (UK) EMA / European Commission (EU)


Core new-drug application NDA under 505(b)(1) or 505(b)(2); BLA under PHS Act 351(a) for biologics[52](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=52)[47](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=47)[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=42) New Drug Submission (NDS)[93](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=93) National UK-wide MAA; full-dossier NAS data under HMR 2012 reg. 50(5)[119](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/rolling-review-for-marketing-authorisation-applications)[229](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines) Centralised MAA under Reg. 726/2004 (mandatory for Annex products, optional for new active substances and innovations); national, MRP or DCP routes under Dir. 2001/83/EC[363](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_3)[221](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02001L0083-20250101#art_28)


Dossier format CTD; electronic submissions must use an FDA-supported eCTD version[264](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=264)[280](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=280) Electronic filing required (eCTD or non-eCTD electronic-only); Canadian Module 1[19](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/applications-submissions/guidance-documents/filing-submissions-electronically.html)[6](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=6) Complete eCTD with UK-specific Module 1 plus Modules 2 to 5[125](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines) CTD format mandated by Annex I for all application types and procedures[2](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02001L0083-20250101#anx_I)


Standard review target 10 months (NME NDAs and original BLAs: from the 60-day filing date)[236](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=236) 300 calendar days review, after 55 days processing and screening[93](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=93) Positive decision possible within 150 clock-on days; final decision aimed within 210 clock-on days[229](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines)[125](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines) CHMP opinion within 210 days of a valid application, then Commission decision[202](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_6)[257](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_10)


Faster standard-track option Priority review: 6 months[234](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=234)[236](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=236) Priority Review: 180-day review, 215 days in total[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=60) IRP Recognition A (60 days) or Recognition B (110 days); Access NASWSI work-sharing; rolling review[125](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines)[181](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/rolling-review-for-marketing-authorisation-applications) Accelerated assessment: 150 days[203](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_14)


Conditional / surrogate-based approval Accelerated approval with confirmatory trials[318](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=318) NOC with Conditions (NOC/c)[144](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=144) Conditional MA, valid for one year and renewable[171](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/conditional-marketing-authorisations-exceptional-circumstances-marketing-authorisations-and-national-scientific-advice) Conditional MA (Art. 14a), valid for one year and renewable[255](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_14a)


Rare or incomplete-data route Animal Rule (21 CFR 314.600 and 601.90) where human efficacy studies are not ethical or feasible; one trial plus confirmatory evidence is evidentiary flexibility, not a separate authorisation route[295](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=295) No separate route found in the sources reviewed MA under exceptional circumstances (UK-wide from 1 January 2025)[171](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/conditional-marketing-authorisations-exceptional-circumstances-marketing-authorisations-and-national-scientific-advice) Exceptional circumstances (Art. 14(8)), reassessed annually[203](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_14)


Development-stage support Fast track, breakthrough therapy designation[318](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=318) Pre-submission meetings; advance NOC/c eligibility[98](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=98) ILAP (Innovation Passport)[168](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=168) PRIME[204](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=204)


### Pathway architecture


#### FDA


In the US the pathway depends on how the application is supported rather than on who reviews it. A 505(b)(1) NDA contains full reports of safety and effectiveness investigations conducted by or for the applicant, or for which the applicant has a right of reference[52](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=52) . A 505(b)(2) NDA relies at least in part on studies the applicant did not conduct and has no right of reference to, such as published literature or FDA's prior findings for a listed drug. It requires a scientific bridge to that listed drug[47](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=47)[43](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=43) . Biologics are licensed through a BLA under section 351 of the PHS Act, which requires full reports showing the product is safe, pure and potent[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=42) . A 351(a) BLA cannot rely on FDA's prior findings for another licensed biologic. The abbreviated route for biologics is 351(k)[48](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=48)[55](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=55) .


#### Health Canada


A new drug is filed as an NDS. Supplements are filed as SNDS, and generics as ANDS referencing a Canadian Reference Product[93](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=93)[77](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=77)[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=102) . Health Canada may use foreign reviews and decisions as inputs, from critical assessment of the foreign review to using it as a reference alongside a Canadian assessment. A full Canadian data package is still required, and the Canadian benefit-risk decision remains Health Canada's own[384](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=384)[385](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=385)[389](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=389) . A 2026 draft guidance on a Ministerial Reliance Order describes a route where, for specified drug classes and listed foreign authorities, certain examination requirements can be deemed met on the basis of foreign decisions. The sponsor must file a complete Canadian submission, and Canadian-specific matters such as labelling and risk management plans are still examined[395](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/applications-submissions/guidance-documents/ministerial-reliance-order-decisions-documents-drugs-foreign-regulatory-authorities.html)[403](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/applications-submissions/guidance-documents/ministerial-reliance-order-decisions-documents-drugs-foreign-regulatory-authorities.html) .


#### MHRA


Since leaving the EU framework, the UK runs its own national procedure for innovative medicines. It uses fixed monthly submission and assessment timetables built around consultation with the Commission on Human Medicines (CHM)[125](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines) . Alongside it, the International Recognition Procedure (IRP) lets applicants use approvals from reference regulators in Australia, Canada, the EU, Japan, Switzerland, Singapore and the United States. The IRP started alongside the national procedures on 1 January 2024[345](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/international-recognition-procedure) . IRP applications must concern the same product as the reference regulator approved, and must include all iterations of that regulator's assessment reports[224](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=224)[225](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=225) . UK paediatric requirements still apply under every route, including the IRP[228](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/procedures-for-uk-paediatric-investigation-plan-pips) . The IRP has its own requirements and timelines, separate from national assessment[229](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines) . Recognition B submission dates line up with CHM dates for new active substances[347](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/international-recognition-procedure) . Recognition A is a 60-day timetable with no clock-stop. Recognition B is a 110-day timetable with a clock-stop at day 70; the applicant generally has up to 60 days to respond.


#### EU


A product listed in the Annex to Regulation 726/2004 cannot be placed on the EU market without a Union authorisation granted through the centralised procedure[363](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_3) . Products outside the Annex can opt in if they contain an active substance not authorised in the Union on 20 May 2004. They can also opt in if the applicant shows significant therapeutic, scientific or technical innovation, or that Union authorisation is in the interest of patients' health at Union level[363](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_3) . Other products go through national procedures or two multi-state routes under Directive 2001/83/EC:


- Mutual recognition (MRP), for products already authorised in a Member State. The reference Member State has 90 days to prepare or update its assessment report, and concerned Member States then have 90 days to approve[221](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02001L0083-20250101#art_28) .
- Decentralised procedure (DCP), for products not yet authorised anywhere. The reference Member State has 120 days to prepare draft documents, followed by 90 days for concerned Member States[221](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02001L0083-20250101#art_28) .


In both cases, national decisions follow within 30 days of agreement[221](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02001L0083-20250101#art_28) .


### Data requirements


#### Common structure


All four agencies use the five-module CTD. Module 1 is regional and administrative. Modules 2 to 5 hold the summaries, quality data, nonclinical reports and clinical study reports, and are meant to be common across regions[264](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=264)[265](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=265)[6](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=6)[2](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02001L0083-20250101#anx_I)[125](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines) . The EU's Annex I applies the CTD to all application types, full or abridged, under any procedure[2](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02001L0083-20250101#anx_I) . Region-specific content goes in Module 1. Canada, for example, requires Health Canada summaries, an environmental assessment statement and electronic review documents there, and puts a product's status in other jurisdictions in Module 1.2.7[6](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=6)[25](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=25) .


#### Evidentiary standard for effectiveness


- **FDA:** The statute requires "substantial evidence of effectiveness" from adequate and well-controlled investigations[306](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=306) . FDA has generally read this as two independently convincing trials. It may accept one adequate and well-controlled trial plus confirmatory evidence, decided case by case based on the persuasiveness of the trial, the strength of the confirmatory evidence, and the disease context[295](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=295)[292](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=292) . Substantial evidence is necessary but not sufficient for approval: FDA must also find the drug safe and its benefits greater than its risks[306](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=306) . A June 2026 draft guidance consolidates these approaches[300](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=300) .
- **Health Canada:** Under the Priority Review policy, substantial evidence of clinical effectiveness usually means at least two adequate, well-controlled studies. One large study, or one pivotal study plus additional clinical evidence, may be considered in some cases[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=67) .
- **EU:** Article 8(3) of Directive 2001/83/EC requires results of pharmaceutical, pre-clinical and clinical trials with detailed summaries[222](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02001L0083-20250101#art_8) . It also requires a pharmacovigilance system summary, a risk management plan, a statement that non-EU trials met EU ethical requirements, and copies of other marketing authorisations and any refusals[222](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02001L0083-20250101#art_8)[382](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02001L0083-20250101#art_8) . The active-substance manufacturer must also have been audited for GMP compliance, with written confirmation[222](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02001L0083-20250101#art_8) .
- **MHRA:** MHRA refuses applications at technical-completeness stage if the data required by HMR 2012 regulations 49 to 55 and Schedule 8 are missing[125](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines) . Every MAA must include a risk management plan. The finished-product manufacturer must hold a valid manufacturing authorisation and GMP certificate before grant[115](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/licensing-procedure-for-electronic-cigarettes-as-medicines) .


#### Abridged routes and regulatory protection


Each system separates full-dossier applications from reliance-based ones:


- **FDA:** 505(b)(2) and ANDA routes for drugs, and 351(k) for biosimilars[47](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=47)[55](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=55) . New chemical entities receive 5 years of exclusivity. Certain NDA approvals can receive 3 years, and orphan-designated indications 7 years[378](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=378)[379](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=379) .
- **Health Canada:** An innovative drug receives 8 years of data protection from its first NOC. This includes a 6-year no-file period for comparative submissions, and can be extended by 6 months for qualifying paediatric studies[365](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/applications-submissions/guidance-documents/guidance-document-data-protection-under-08-004-1-food-drug-regulations.html)[366](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/applications-submissions/guidance-documents/guidance-document-data-protection-under-08-004-1-food-drug-regulations.html) .
- **EU:** Generic, hybrid and similar-biological routes exist under Article 10[1](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02001L0083-20250101#art_10) . Centrally authorised products get 8 years of data exclusivity and 10 years of market protection. Market protection extends to 11 years if a new indication with significant clinical benefit is approved within the first 8 years[203](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_14)[1](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02001L0083-20250101#art_10) .
- **UK:** Generic (reg. 51B), biosimilar (reg. 53B) and well-established-use (reg. 54) bases are available alongside the full-dossier reg. 50(5) route[119](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/rolling-review-for-marketing-authorisation-applications)[129](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=129) .


### Review timelines


Headline numbers are not directly comparable, because each agency starts and stops its clock differently.


- **FDA:** Under PDUFA the goal is to review and act on 90% of standard NME NDAs and original BLAs within 10 months of the 60-day filing date, and priority ones within 6 months of it[236](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=236) . For non-NME NDAs the clock runs from receipt[236](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=236) . "Act" means an approval letter or a complete response letter; meeting the goal does not mean approval[236](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=236) . Priority designation is decided within 60 days of receipt and assigned at filing[234](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=234) .
- **Health Canada:** The standard NDS target is 10 days processing, 45 days screening and 300 days review[93](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=93) . Priority Review cuts these to 25 days screening and 180 days review, for a 215-day total. Responses to a priority Notice of Non-compliance have a 125-day target[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=60) . All targets are in calendar days[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=60) .
- **MHRA:** For innovative medicines, MHRA completes its initial assessment by Day 90 and then issues a consolidated request for information (RFI), which stops the clock. Applicants normally have up to 6 months to respond[125](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines) . MHRA assesses the response by Day 150. If all issues are resolved, a positive decision is possible within 150 clock-on days. Otherwise MHRA aims for a final decision within 210 clock-on days[125](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines)[229](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines) . Timetables are in calendar days excluding clock-stops[229](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines) . MHRA refuses an MA only after final CHM advice, unless the applicant has failed to respond to an RFI in time[125](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines) .
- **EU:** The CHMP must give its opinion within 210 days of a valid application. Scientific analysis normally takes at least 80 days[202](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_6) . The Commission then prepares a draft decision within 15 days of the opinion and adopts the final decision within 15 days of the Standing Committee's opinion[257](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_10) .


### Expedited and conditional mechanisms


#### Development-stage designations


FDA's fast track requires data showing potential to address an unmet need in a serious condition. Breakthrough therapy requires preliminary clinical evidence of substantial improvement over available therapy. Both include rolling review, and FDA generally responds to designation requests within 60 days[318](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=318)[234](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=234) . EMA's PRIME is a voluntary scheme based on early clinical data showing potential benefit in unmet need. It provides an early CHMP or CAT rapporteur, a kick-off meeting and scientific advice at key milestones[204](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=204) . The UK's ILAP is open to developers of potentially transformative medicines that have evidence of safe use in humans but have not yet started confirmatory trials. It brings in MHRA, HTA bodies and the NHS[168](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=168)[167](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/statement-of-policy-intent-relaunch-of-the-innovative-licensing-and-access-pathway) . MHRA's rolling review assesses dossier modules iteratively. Each module is assessed within 60 days of validation, and the final phase is structured as 100 days (60 + 40 days)[181](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/rolling-review-for-marketing-authorisation-applications)[288](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/rolling-review-for-marketing-authorisation-applications) .


#### Shortened standard review


Examples are FDA priority review (6 months versus 10)[234](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=234) , Health Canada Priority Review (180 days versus 300)[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=60) and EU accelerated assessment (150 days versus 210)[203](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_14) . Their criteria are similar but not the same:


- **FDA:** A significant improvement in safety or effectiveness for a serious condition[318](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=318) .
- **Health Canada:** A serious, life-threatening or severely debilitating condition, plus either no drug therapy marketed in Canada or a clinically relevant improvement in benefit-risk over marketed therapies[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=60)[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=62) . The request, with a Clinical Assessment Package, must be filed before the submission. Health Canada decides within 30 days, and the NDS must then be filed within 60 days[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=66)[73](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=73) .
- **EU:** Major public-health interest, particularly therapeutic innovation[203](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_14) .


#### Approval on less-than-complete evidence


- **FDA accelerated approval:** Based on a surrogate or intermediate clinical endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit. Confirmatory trials are required, and the approval can be withdrawn on an expedited basis[318](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=318) .
- **Health Canada NOC/c:** Based on promising evidence of clinical effectiveness for serious conditions, and applies to the specific indication[144](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=144)[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=151) . Before authorisation the sponsor signs a Letter of Undertaking committing to confirmatory trials, enhanced surveillance and advertising disclosures[142](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=142)[146](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=146)[155](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=155) . The advance-consideration pathway has a 200-day review target. After an NOC/c Qualifying Notice, the sponsor has 30 days to respond and Health Canada has 30 days to finalise the conditions[98](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=98) . SNDS-C filings with confirmatory results get no reduced review target[143](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=143) .
- **EU conditional MA (Article 14a):** For seriously debilitating or life-threatening diseases where immediate availability outweighs the risk of outstanding data. It carries specific obligations reviewed annually, and is valid for one year and renewable. It can convert to a standard five-year authorisation once the obligations are fulfilled[255](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_14a) .
- **UK conditional MA:** Mirrors the EU concept. It requires unmet medical need, a positive benefit-risk balance and a one-year renewable validity, and can convert to a standard MA once obligations are met[171](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/conditional-marketing-authorisations-exceptional-circumstances-marketing-authorisations-and-national-scientific-advice)[173](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/conditional-marketing-authorisations-exceptional-circumstances-marketing-authorisations-and-national-scientific-advice) .
- **Exceptional circumstances (EU and UK):** For cases where comprehensive data cannot be provided, for example because the condition is rare. The EU route requires objective, verifiable reasons and annual reassessment[203](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_14) . In the UK this route normally does not lead to a standard MA, and applicants must discuss it with MHRA before applying[171](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/conditional-marketing-authorisations-exceptional-circumstances-marketing-authorisations-and-national-scientific-advice)[176](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/conditional-marketing-authorisations-exceptional-circumstances-marketing-authorisations-and-national-scientific-advice) .


### Practical implications for global filing strategy


- **One core dossier, four Module 1s.** CTD Modules 2 to 5 carry over across all four agencies. Regional effort goes into Module 1, labelling, and region-specific items such as UK paediatric documentation and Canadian environmental assessment statements[264](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=264)[6](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=6)[228](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/procedures-for-uk-paediatric-investigation-plan-pips) .
- **Normalise the clocks before comparing.** FDA's clock for NMEs starts after a 60-day filing period[236](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=236) . Health Canada adds a screening phase before review[93](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=93) . MHRA and the EU count days of active assessment, and elapsed time also depends on how quickly the sponsor answers RFIs[125](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/national-assessment-procedure-for-medicines)[202](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02004R0726-20220128#art_6) .
- **Sequencing can be used deliberately.** An FDA or EU approval can later support filings through MHRA's IRP[345](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/international-recognition-procedure) and Health Canada's use of foreign reviews[385](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=385)[390](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/applications-submissions/guidance-documents/use-foreign-reviews/frequently-asked-questions-use-foreign-reviews.html) . Health Canada notes that foreign reviews may sometimes allow a faster-than-typical review, but Canadian standards still apply[390](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/applications-submissions/guidance-documents/use-foreign-reviews/frequently-asked-questions-use-foreign-reviews.html) .
- **Line up expedited requests early.** Health Canada requires the priority request before filing[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=66) . FDA designations are requested during development[234](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=234) . PRIME and ILAP are entered before confirmatory trials[204](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=204)[168](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/new-drug-marketing-authorisation-compared-fda?showSourceNumber=168) .


The Annex to Regulation 726/2004 makes the centralised procedure mandatory for specified classes, including certain biotechnology products, orphan medicines and advanced-therapy products.
